title: Health Information Bill Second Reading debate
what_it_is: A Second Reading debate on the Health Information Bill, which requires licensed healthcare providers and retail pharmacies to contribute key health information to the National Electronic Health Record and sets rules for access, sharing and safeguards.
why_it_matters: The Bill requires all licensed healthcare providers and retail pharmacies to contribute key health information to NEHR, so a patient's records can follow them across providers. It allows patients to restrict access, while critical allergies and vaccination records remain visible, and prohibits access for employment or insurance purposes. The Minister says the Bill is intended to take effect from early 2027.

key_points.point: The Health Information Bill was moved for Second Reading.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: The Bill be now read a Second time.

key_points.point: Singapore is ageing rapidly, with one in four Singaporeans aged 65 and above by 2030.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: By 2030, one in four Singaporeans will be aged 65 and above.

key_points.point: Currently, key health records are often not accessible across providers, which can risk medication errors, delayed treatment and duplicate tests.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: Such gaps can risk medication errors, delayed treatment and duplicate tests and procedures.

key_points.point: The Bill requires all licensed healthcare providers and retail pharmacies to contribute key health information to NEHR.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: The HIB will require all healthcare providers licensed under the Healthcare Services Act 2020 and retail pharmacies licensed under the Health Products Act 2007 to contribute key health information about patients into NEHR.

key_points.point: Key health information includes allergies, vaccinations, diagnoses, medications, laboratory test results, radiological images and discharge summaries.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: allergies, vaccinations, diagnoses, medications, laboratory test results, radiological images and discharge summaries

key_points.point: NEHR access for patient care is limited to licensed healthcare providers and their authorised individuals.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: NEHR access for patient care purposes will be limited to licensed healthcare providers and their authorised individuals.

key_points.point: Accessing NEHR for employment or insurance purposes is strictly prohibited.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: Accessing NEHR for purposes relating to employment or insurance will be strictly prohibited.

key_points.point: NEHR access is allowed for specified statutory medical examinations.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: NEHR access will therefore be allowed for these statutory medical examinations.

key_points.point: Patients may restrict access to their NEHR information so that only select healthcare providers may have access.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: they may restrict access to their NEHR information so that only select healthcare providers may have this access.

key_points.point: From the second half of this year, patients can place an Access Restriction through the HealthHub app.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: From the second half of this year, patients can do so through the HealthHub app.

key_points.point: During medical emergencies, a patient's NEHR information may be accessed despite an Access Restriction, with only doctors allowed to 'break glass'.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: only doctors will be allowed to "break glass".

key_points.point: Non-NEHR health information may be shared without consent only if three key criteria are met.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: We will enable the scoped sharing of non-NEHR health information without an individual's consent only if three key criteria are met.

key_points.point: A first offence for unauthorised access of NEHR information under clause 38 carries a fine of up to $50,000, two years' imprisonment or both.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: a person convicted of an offence relating to unauthorised access of NEHR information under clause 38 faces a fine of up to $50,000, two years’ imprisonment or both, for a first offence.

key_points.point: Healthcare providers that fail to put in place required cybersecurity or data security measures may face a fine of up to $1 million.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: healthcare providers that fail to put in place the cybersecurity or data security measures required under the HIB may face a fine of up to $1 million

key_points.point: The Bill is intended to take effect from early 2027.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: we intend for the Bill to take effect from early 2027.

key_points.point: The Health Government Parliamentary Committee supports the Bill.
key_points.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
key_points.quote: The Health Government Parliamentary Committee (GPC) supports this Bill.

key_points.point: Dennis Tan supports the Bill but raises concerns about challenges for smaller healthcare operators such as single or dual-doctor clinics.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
key_points.quote: while I support the Bill, I wish to raise a few concerns posed by the HIB, and I will be speaking on the challenges for smaller healthcare operators, such as single or dual-doctor practitioner clinics that many of my residents rely on for their daily medical needs.

key_points.point: Dennis Tan says the $1 million cap effectively puts a ceiling on the value of the collective privacy of the nation.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
key_points.quote: the $1 million cap effectively puts a ceiling on the value of the collective privacy of the nation

key_points.point: Dr Wan Rizal strongly supports the safeguard disallowing health data from being accessed or used for employment purposes.
key_points.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
key_points.quote: I strongly support the safeguard in this Bill that disallows health data from being accessed or used for employment purposes.

key_points.point: Louis Chua says insurers cannot access NEHR directly, but asks whether transcription and audit clauses could let them access NEHR-derived information in clinical notes.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
key_points.quote: Today, insurers cannot access NEHR, but perhaps through transcription and audit clauses, they can access NEHR-derived information sitting in clinical notes.

key_points.point: Kenneth Tiong says a Bill that compels contribution must also come with robust ecosystem safeguards.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
key_points.quote: a Bill that compels contribution must also come with robust ecosystem safeguards.

key_points.point: Joan Pereira seeks comprehensive onboarding support for GPs, including shared staffing arrangements for small clinics.
key_points.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
key_points.quote: comprehensive onboarding support for GPs, including innovative shared staffing arrangements for small clinics

key_points.point: Kuah Boon Theng says the Workgroup she co-chaired completed its work and issued guidelines on national health records.
key_points.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng
key_points.quote: The Workgroup, which I co-chaired, has since completed its work and issued a set of guidelines

key_points.point: Dr Choo Pei Ling says allied health professionals play indispensable roles and should have access to relevant NEHR information.
key_points.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling
key_points.quote: AHPs – physiotherapists, radiographers, occupational therapists, speech and language therapists and radiation therapists – play indispensable roles in patient care and should have access to relevant NEHR information.

key_points.point: Dr Haresh Singaraju says clause 99 protects those acting in good faith and with reasonable care but does not define what reasonable care looks like.
key_points.speaker: Dr Haresh Singaraju
key_points.quote: Clause 99 protects those who act in good faith and with reasonable care, but it does not define what reasonable care looks like.

key_points.point: David Hoe asks what assisted pathways will be available for residents who wish to understand and manage access restrictions.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Hoe
key_points.quote: I wonder what assisted pathways will be available for residents who wish to understand and also know how they can manage their access restrictions?

key_points.point: Dr Hamid Razak asks the Minister to confirm that NEHR is a supplementary clinical tool, not a mandatory step in every consultation.
key_points.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak
key_points.quote: Can the Minister confirm that the NEHR is positioned as a supplementary clinical tool, and not a mandatory step that must be accessed in every single consultation?

key_points.point: In response, the Senior Minister of State says Synapxe is not a commercial entity.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: Synapxe is not a commercial entity.

key_points.point: The Senior Minister of State says insurers and employers do not and will not have access to NEHR.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: insurers and employers do not and will not have access to NEHR.

key_points.point: The Senior Minister of State says there are no plans to expand the list of statutory medical examinations to employment-related screenings not necessary to protect the public and the individual.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: We have no plans to expand this list to include employment-related screenings that are not necessary to protect the public and the individual.

key_points.point: The Senior Minister of State says accessing patients' NEHR information is not compulsory under the Bill.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: Accessing patients' NEHR information is not compulsory under the HIB.

key_points.point: The Senior Minister of State says support packages will defray costs of subscription to whitelisted HIB-compliant health information management systems.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: Our support package will include measures to defray costs of subscription to whitelisted HIB-compliant HIMS

key_points.point: The Senior Minister of State says the Bill will commence in early 2027 to allow sufficient time for familiarisation.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: the Bill will commence in early 2027 to allow sufficient time for healthcare providers and professionals to familiarise themselves with the Bill's requirements.

key_points.point: The Senior Minister of State says guidance materials and dedicated support channels will be available from the second quarter of this year.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: guidance materials and dedicated support channels will be made available from the second quarter of this year

key_points.point: In a clarification, the Senior Minister of State says access to NEHR, even through EMR, will be logged as an access to NEHR.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: Access to NEHR, even through the EMR, will be logged as an access to NEHR.

what_happens_next: The Bill is intended to commence from early 2027, and MOH will announce further implementation details soon.
not_said: Whether the maximum fine of $1 million is sufficient to deter large healthcare organisations.
How MOH will ensure insurers cannot obtain NEHR-derived information through clinical notes or audit clauses.
What the exact funding quantum and eligibility criteria will be for small GP clinics.
Whether cybersecurity insurance will be offered to small providers.
How patients who are not digitally confident will be assisted to place or manage Access Restrictions.
When and whether community health partners beyond public entities will be added to the Fourth Schedule.
How overseas medical records will be treated in the NEHR.
What constitutes 'reasonable access' to NEHR for clinicians in practice.
How data breach notification thresholds will apply to smaller breaches.
Whether the list of statutory medical examinations will remain tightly scoped over time.
